# Adjudication Task — Chapter 655

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃655화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|남만은 중원과 분리된 소국(小國)과 같고, 남만야수궁은 한 나라의 중심이라 할 수 있는 왕궁이다.
  6|
  7|당연히 내궁 역시 그 규모가 거대할 수밖에 없었다.
  8|
  9|전사, 숙수, 하인, 맹수들을 관리하는 사육사 등 내궁에 머무르는 이들의 머릿수를 모두 합하면 일천에 달하고, 지금처럼 부족 대회의가 열리는 상황에서는 몇 배로 불어난다.
 10|
 11|하지만 그 수많은 사람 사이에서도 가장 중요한 이들은 따로 있었다.
 12|
 13|바로 네 명의 대족장들이다.
 14|
 15|남만에 존재하는 서른두 개 부족 중 가장 강성한 네 개의 부족을 이끌고 있으며, 차기 남만야수궁주가 될 수 있는 실력자들.
 16|
 17|그런 만큼 대족장들이 가진 영향력은 막강했고, 궁주를 제외한 세 명의 대족장들은 대대로 특혜를 보장받았다.
 18|
 19|쉬쉬쉭!
 20|
 21|현재 옆에서 내달리는 야율목이 하는 말처럼.
 22|
 23|“아버님을 제외한 모든 부족장은 각 부족의 본거지에 머무르며 사전에 통보를 해야만 내궁에 출입할 수 있지만, 대족장들만큼은 예외다. 그들에게는 자유로운 통행과 함께 내궁의 거처가 주어지지.”
 24|
 25|동(東), 서(西), 남(南), 북(北).
 26|
 27|북쪽은 대대로 남만야수궁주가 맡았고, 다른 대족장들은 각 방위에 저마다의 거처를 마련했다고 했다.
 28|
 29|고위 인물에게 내리는 일종의 관저(官邸)인 동시에, 중원식으로 해석하자면 천자가 휘하 제후에게 왕부(王府)를 여는 것을 허락해 준 셈이다.
 30|
 31|하지만 지금 이 순간.
 32|
 33|전력을 다해 달려온 나를 기다리고 있던 것은 흥건하게 고여 있는 핏물과 시신, 그리고 누군가에 의해 파괴된 건물의 잔해였다.
 34|
 35|“이게 무슨…….”
 36|
 37|귓가를 파고드는 남호의 침음성. 나는 전신의 피가 싸늘하게 식는 듯한 느낌을 받으며 고개를 들었다.
 38|
 39|부서진 대문 위로 기울어져 있는 목판과 글씨가 보였다.
 40|
 41|서요부(西瑤部).
 42|
 43|이 장원이 누구의 소유인지 알려 주는 세 글자. 문득 고혹적인 눈웃음을 짓던 어느 여인의 모습이 눈앞을 스쳤다.
 44|
 45|‘요족의 대족장. 요희.’
 46|
 47|아름다움이라는 단어보다는 요사스럽다는 말이 더 어울리는 여인.
 48|
 49|그녀가 정말 오늘 밤 벌어진 습격의 흉수인지는 모르겠지만, 두 가지 사실만은 확실하다.
 50|
 51|요희의 취향이 듬뿍 들어간 이 화려한 장원은 더 이상 전처럼 아름답지 않다는 것.
 52|
 53|그리고 씻은 듯이 자취를 감추었다는 것.
 54|
 55|저벅.
 56|
 57|반쯤 부서진 대문을 넘어 들어서자, 곳곳에 널브러진 시신과 맹수들의 사체가 보인다.
 58|
 59|각자의 색을 지니고 있었을 형형색색의 꽃밭은 온통 붉은 핏물에 물들어 있었다.
 60|
 61|“……시벌.”
 62|
 63|참지 못하고 욕설을 중얼거린 그때, 나와 함께 나란히 걸어 들어오는 야율목을 발견한 전사 중 하나가 다가왔다.
 64|
 65|“오셨습니까, 소궁주.”
 66|
 67|야율목이 굳은 얼굴로 고개를 끄덕였다.
 68|
 69|“고생이 많다. 추가로 발견된 점은?”
 70|
 71|“없습니다. 시신이 늘었다는 것을 빼면요.”
 72|
 73|무거운 목소리로 대답한 전사의 등 뒤로, 나란히 누워 있는 시신들이 보인다. 몇 걸음 떨어지지 않은 우물에서는 서너 명의 전사가 물에 젖어 축 늘어진 호랑이를 끌어 올리는 중이었다.
 74|
 75|“지금까지 확인된 숫자만 말씀드리자면, 요족 전사와 그들이 부리는 맹수들을 합쳐 족히 일백을 헤아립니다.”
 76|
 77|“생존자는?”
 78|
 79|야율목의 물음에 잠시 침묵하던 전사가 대답했다.
 80|
 81|“……현재로서는 전무합니다.”
 82|
 83|현재로서는?
 84|
 85|글쎄. 내 생각에는 앞으로도 전무할 것 같은데.
 86|
 87|내심 중얼거린 나는 누워 있는 시신들을 향해 다가갔다.
 88|
 89|반사적으로 앞을 막아서려던 전사가 나와 눈이 마주치자 움찔하며 물러났고, 나는 시신들의 몸에 난 상흔(傷痕)을 살폈다.
 90|
 91|이들이 어떤 방식으로 의문의 습격자와 싸웠는지, 또 어떻게 죽음을 맞이했는지.
 92|
 93|그리고 깨달음과 동시에 야율목의 목소리가 들려왔다.
 94|
 95|“알아낸 것이 있나?
 96|
 97|동시에 이쪽을 향해 쏠리는 수십여 쌍의 시선을 느끼며, 나는 짤막하게 대꾸했다.
 98|
 99|“강기(罡氣).”
100|
101|“……!”
102|
103|“……!”
104|
105|보이지 않는 동요가 퍼져 나간다. 나는 딱딱한 목소리로 말을 이었다.
106|
107|“상대는 틀림없이 초절정 고수야. 이들 중 대부분은 마지막 순간까지 기습을 눈치채지 못했겠지. 그만큼 무공의 격차가 컸을 테니까.”
108|
109|초절정은 극소수의 선택받은 자들에게만 허락된 영역.
110|
111|무수한 고난 끝에 벽을 넘어 위대한 경지로 발돋움한 초절정 고수들은 말 그대로 초인(超人)이 된다.
112|
113|단 한 번 검을 휘둘러 일류 고수 수십을 죽일 수도 있고, 적수공권으로도 십여 명의 절정 고수를 피떡으로 만들 수 있는 이들.
114|
115|오늘 밤, 이곳을 습격한 흉수가 바로 그랬다.
116|
117|‘극히 빠르고 간결하며, 더할 나위 없이 치명적인 솜씨.’
118|
119|시신들에 남아 있는 상흔을 보자마자 알아차렸다. 흉수는 닳고 닳은 살인자라는 것을.
120|
121|놈은 결코 부족하지도, 그렇다고 과하지도 않은 힘으로 장원 안의 모든 생명체를 도륙했다.
122|
123|일 촌(寸)의 깊이만으로도 목숨을 빼앗을 수 있다는 것은 천하 무림의 모두가 아는 사실이지만, 그렇게 일백을 헤아리는 전사와 맹수를 몰살시킬 수 있는 것은 초절정 고수뿐이다.
124|
125|그리고 이것이 의미하는 바는 분명했다.
126|
127|- 이 모든 것이, 백상의 소행이라는 거냐?
128|
129|귓가를 파고드는 나직한 전음(傳音). 나는 충격에 휩싸인 사람들 사이로 딱딱하게 굳어 있는 야율목의 얼굴을 바라보았다.
130|
131|- 글쎄.
132|
133|- 글쎄라니?
134|
135|- 남만에서 이 정도의 경지에 다다른 고수는 둘밖에 없어. 한 명은 알다시피 백상이고. 다른 한 사람은……. 남만의 모두가 잘 아는 사람이지.
136|
137|순간, 야율목의 얼굴이 새하얗게 질리는 것이 보였다. 소리라도 지를 듯이 입을 크게 벌린 녀석이 입술을 질끈 깨물었다.
138|
139|- 너는, 이 일의 흉수가 아버님이라고 말하고 싶은 건가?
140|
141|- 그럴 리가.
142|
143|- 그렇다면 왜…….
144|
145|- 이대로면 너무 뻔하다는 얘기지. 최소한 암천이 직접 개입했다는 건 확실하고.
146|
147|초절정 고수는 중원에서도 극히 드문 수준의 고수지만, 남만에서는 더더욱 그렇다. 개인적으로 백상에 대한 의심이 있다고는 해도 이 정도의 돌대가리는 아니다.
148|
149|아마도 최소한 암천에 소속된 초절정 고수를 동원했겠지.
150|
151|‘한 발자국 떨어져서 상황을 지켜보는 것 같더니, 드디어 직접 나선 건가?’
152|
153|하지만 무엇을 노리고?
154|
155|머릿속에 떠오른 의문을 내심 중얼거린 나는, 전음 대신 소리 내어 물었다.
156|
157|“직접 확인해 보고 싶은 게 있는데. 잠깐 자리를 옮길까?”
158|
159|내 말뜻을 알아들은 야율목이 눈짓하자 주위의 시선들이 떨어져 나간다.
160|
161|나와 야율목, 그리고 남호까지. 우리 셋은 장원의 중심에 위치한 전각 내부로 들어갔다.
162|
163|그리고 모두가 예상했던 대로 온갖 진귀한 집기로 가득했을 그곳은 한바탕 폭풍우라도 휩쓸고 지나간 것처럼 엉망이었다.
164|
165|“한판 제대로 붙은 모양이군.”
166|
167|남호의 중얼거림에 야율목이 굳은 얼굴로 대답했다.
168|
169|“하지만 전투는 불과 촌각 만에 끝났소. 상대가 초절정 고수였으니 당연했겠지.”
170|
171|“자네가 그걸 어찌 아나?”
172|
173|“짧지만 분명한 굉음이 들렸으니까. 내가 보고를 듣고 도착했을 때는 이미 모든 것이 끝난 후였소. 요서부에 남아 있던 것은 피와 시체, 그리고…….”
174|
175|드르륵.
176|
177|커다란 미닫이문을 열어젖힌 야율목이, 가라앉은 목소리로 말을 이었다.
178|
179|“저것들뿐이었지.”
180|
181|야율목이 ‘저것들’이라 부른 것은 두 개의 물건이었다.
182|
183|난장판이 된 방 안에 떨어져 있는 향낭(香囊). 그리고 쓰임새는 그보다 더 귀하고, 끔찍한 향을 풍기는 무언가.
184|
185|“으음.”
186|
187|남호는 침음성을 흘렸고, 나는 망설임 없이 걸음을 옮겨 ‘그것’에 손을 댔다. 차갑게 식은 촉감과 함께 끈적한 핏물이 내 손가락을 적신다.
188|
189|‘이건.’
190|
191|눈이 달린 사람이라면 누구라도 알아볼 수 있는 물건이다.
192|
193|‘그것’의 정체는 손목이었다. 깔끔하게 잘려 나간 누군가의 손목.
194|
195|“누구의 것인지 알아볼 수 있겠나?”
196|
197|못 알아볼 리가.
198|
199|투실투실하게 살이 오른 손목을 말없이 응시하던 나는, 야율목의 물음에 나직한 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
200|
201|“아마도 흑웅이겠지.”
202|
203|“맞다. 호위 넷을 데리고 요희 대족장을 찾았다더군. 동이부(東夷部)에서 확인해 주었다.”
204|
205|요족이 서쪽에 서요부를 세웠다면, 흑웅이 이끄는 이족은 동쪽에 자리 잡아 동이부를 세운 모양이었다. 나는 흑웅의 손목을 내려놓으며 물었다.
206|
207|“그때 시각은?”
208|
209|“반 시진은 넘지 않았고, 한 식경은 족히 지났다더군.”
210|
211|대충 시간을 가늠해 보니 나와 헤어진 직후다. 우선 바로 동이부로 갔다가 요희를 찾아간 것이 틀림없었다.
212|
213|‘……이 미친 사랑꾼 새끼. 그새를 못 참고.’
214|
215|나는 입 밖으로 튀어나오려는 욕설을 참기 위해 안간힘을 써야 했다. 지금은 냉정해야 할 때다.
216|
217|아직 흑웅이 요희를 찾아간 이유도 모를뿐더러, 죽음이 확인되지 않은 이상은 모두를 의심해 봐야 했으니까.
218|
219|“흑웅이 데려왔다는 호위들은?”
220|
221|“죽었다. 다른 요족 전사들과 함께.”
222|
223|그럼 그렇지, 씨발.
224|
225|혹시나 해서 물어본 건데, 역시는 역시다.
226|
227|“후우.”
228|
229|깊은 한숨을 내쉰 나는 방 안을 천천히 살폈다.
230|
231|난장판이 된 내부에는 저항의 흔적이 곳곳에 남아 있었고, 아마도 강력한 장력(掌力)에 의해 무너졌을 벽면 너머에는 아직 화려한 모습을 유지하고 있는 후원이 보였다.
232|
233|그곳에 남아 있는 아주 희미한 족적(足跡)도 함께.
234|
235|‘신속하게 두 사람을 제압하고, 후원을 통해 빠져나갔군.’
236|
237|비록 흔적이 너무 희미한 탓에 주인을 알아볼 수는 없지만, 족적을 통해 한 가지만큼은 확실해졌다.
238|
239|흑웅이나 요희, 두 사람 중 하나가 벌인 자작극이 아니라 제삼자가 개입했다는 것.
240|
241|불과 한 식경 전, 이 자리에는 적어도 세 사람이 있었다.
242|
243|‘그중 한 사람은 당연히 초절정 고수고.’
244|
245|그렇다면 이 족적의 주인은 누구일까. 남천마후? 아니면 그녀가 거느리고 있는 암천의 고수?
246|
247|잠시 생각해 보던 나는 이내 고개를 저었다.
248|
249|내가 잔뼈 굵은 노강호도 아니고, 이 정도 단서로 얻을 수 있는 정보에는 한계가 있었다.
250|
251|내 옆에는 은영각 요원으로 활동하며 수많은 정보를 접한 남호가 있긴 하지만, 그건 마두의 용모파기나 외적인 특징에 한해서일 뿐이다.
252|
253|‘결국 무공과 식견, 둘 다 높은 수준에 있는 사람이 필요하다는 건데.’
254|
255|당장 머릿속에 떠오르는 이름은 두 개뿐이었고, 그중 하나는 도무지 믿지 못할 사람이다.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

## Adjudicator rules

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

For `REPAIR`, write the smallest complete replacement needed for that hunk. It must be natural English and fully source-faithful.

## Glossary

Korean **keys** are binding unless the source uses that string in a different ordinary-language sense. Glossary **English** is not a license for a calque (`presiding chair`). If SOL is a natural recast of the same sense, keep SOL.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.

*Yohi. Great Chieftain of the Yao people.*

[P19]
“Bewitching” suited her better than “beautiful.”

[P20]
I didn’t know whether she was behind tonight’s attack, but two things were certain. This splendid estate, so thoroughly shaped by Yohi’s tastes, was no longer as beautiful as it had been.

[P21]
And Yohi herself had vanished without a trace.

[P22]
Step.

[P23]
I crossed through the half-destroyed gate. Bodies lay scattered everywhere, among them the carcasses of beasts. Flower beds that must once have bloomed in all different colors were soaked red with blood.

[P24]
“…Fuck.”

[P25]
I couldn’t keep the curse in. Just then, a warrior spotted Yayul Mok walking beside me and approached.

[P26]
“Young Palace Lord. You’ve arrived.”

[P27]
Yayul Mok nodded, his face grim.

[P28]
“You’ve worked hard. Have you found anything else?”

[P29]
“No. Only more bodies.”

[P30]
Behind the warrior, corpses lay side by side. A few steps away, three or four warriors were hauling a tiger out of a well, its drenched body hanging limp.

[P31]
“So far, we’ve confirmed at least a hundred dead, counting both Yao warriors and the beasts they commanded.”

[P32]
“Any survivors?”

[P33]
The warrior was silent for a moment before answering.

[P34]
“…None so far.”

[P35]
*So far?*

[P36]
I doubted they’d find any. Keeping that thought to myself, I approached the bodies.

[P37]
A warrior instinctively moved to block my way, but when our eyes met, he flinched and stepped aside. I examined the wounds, looking for how these people had fought the unknown attacker—and how they had died.

[P38]
As I realized what had happened, Yayul Mok spoke.

[P39]
“Found anything?”

[P40]
Dozens of pairs of eyes turned toward me. I gave a brief answer.

[P41]
“Force.”

[P42]
“……!”

[P43]
“……!”

[P44]
A ripple of unease passed through the crowd. My voice came out stiff.

[P45]
“The attacker was undoubtedly a Supreme Peak master. Most of them probably didn’t notice the attack until the last moment. The gap in martial arts was that great.”

[P46]
The Supreme Peak realm was open to only a chosen few. After enduring countless hardships and breaking through the barrier, its masters rose to a realm that made them, quite literally, superhuman.

[P47]
With a single swing of a sword, they could kill dozens of First Rate masters. Even barehanded, they could beat a dozen Peak masters to a bloody pulp.

[P48]
Whoever had attacked this place tonight was one of them.

[P49]
*Fast, economical, and utterly lethal.*

[P50]
I’d known as soon as I saw the wounds. The attacker was a seasoned killer.

[P51]
They had slaughtered every living thing in the estate using no more force than necessary, and no less. Everyone in Murim knew that an inch of depth was enough to take a life. Only a Supreme Peak master could kill a hundred warriors and beasts that way.

[P52]
The implication was clear.

[P53]
—Are you saying Baeksang did all this?

[P54]
Yayul Mok’s quiet Sound Transmission reached my ear. I looked at his rigid face amid the shocked crowd.

[P55]
—Who knows?

[P56]
—What do you mean, who knows?

[P57]
—Only two masters in Nanman have reached this level. One is Baeksang, as you know. The other… is someone everyone in Nanman knows well.

[P58]
Yayul Mok went deathly pale. His mouth opened as though he were about to shout, but he bit down hard on his lip instead.

[P59]
—Are you saying Father did this?

[P60]
—Of course not.

[P61]
—Then why…

[P62]
—I’m saying that would be too obvious. What’s certain is that Dark Heaven was directly involved.

[P63]
Supreme Peak masters were exceedingly rare even in the Central Plains, and rarer still in Nanman. I might have my suspicions about Baeksang, but I wasn’t that much of a blockhead.

[P64]
Dark Heaven had probably sent one of its own Supreme Peak masters.

[P65]
*They seemed content to watch from a step away. Have they finally decided to act themselves?*

[P66]
But what were they after?

[P67]
I kept the question to myself and spoke aloud rather than using Sound Transmission.

[P68]
“There’s something I want to check for myself. Shall we step away for a moment?”

[P69]
Yayul Mok understood and gave the onlookers a glance. Their eyes turned away.

[P70]
The three of us—Yayul Mok, Namho, and I—entered the pavilion at the center of the estate. As we’d expected, the place that must once have been filled with rare furnishings looked as though a storm had torn through it.

[P71]
“Looks like they put up a real fight,” Namho muttered.

[P72]
Yayul Mok answered, his face still grim. “But it was over in moments. With a Supreme Peak master against them, I suppose that was inevitable.”

[P73]
“How do you know how long it lasted?”

[P74]
“I heard a brief but unmistakable crash. By the time I received the report and arrived, it was already over. All that remained in the Western Yao Estate was blood, bodies, and…”

[P75]
Rattle.

[P76]
Yayul Mok slid open a large door. His voice sank.

[P77]
“Those.”

[P78]
He meant two things lying in the wrecked room: a scent pouch, and something far more valuable in its use, though it gave off a terrible smell.

[P79]
“Hmm.”

[P80]
Namho let out a low groan. I walked over without hesitation and touched the second object. It was cold, and sticky blood coated my fingers.

[P81]
*This is…*

[P82]
Anyone with eyes would recognize it.

[P83]
A wrist. Someone’s wrist, cleanly severed.

[P84]
“Can you tell whose it is?”

[P85]
How could I not?

[P86]
I stared at the plump wrist for a moment before answering quietly.

[P87]
“Probably Heugung’s.”

[P88]
“That’s right. He came to see Great Chieftain Yohi with four guards. The Eastern Yi Estate confirmed it.”

[P89]
If the Yao people had built the Western Yao Estate in the west, it seemed the Yi people under Heugung had established the Eastern Yi Estate in the east. I set Heugung’s wrist down.

[P90]
“When was that?”

[P91]
“Less than half a shichen ago, but at least half an hour.”

[P92]
I worked out the timing. It was just after Heugung and I had parted. He must have gone straight to the Eastern Yi Estate, then come here to see Yohi.

[P93]
*…That lovesick bastard. He couldn’t wait even that long.*

[P94]
I struggled to keep the curse from coming out. I needed to stay calm.

[P95]
I still didn’t know why Heugung had come to see Yohi. And until his death was confirmed, I had to suspect everyone.

[P96]
“What happened to the guards he brought?”

[P97]
“Dead. Along with the Yao warriors.”

[P98]
*Of course. Fuck.*

[P99]
I’d asked just in case. I’d gotten exactly the answer I expected.

[P100]
“Haa.”

[P101]
I let out a deep breath and slowly surveyed the room. Signs of resistance were everywhere. Beyond a wall that had probably collapsed under a powerful palm strike, I could see a rear garden that had kept its splendor.

[P102]
There were faint footprints there, too.

[P103]
*They subdued the two of them quickly, then escaped through the rear garden.*

[P104]
The prints were too faint to tell me who had left them. But they did establish one thing: this wasn’t an attack staged by Heugung or Yohi. A third party had been here.

[P105]
Less than half an hour ago, at least three people had occupied this room.

[P106]
*And one of them was a Supreme Peak master.*

[P107]
So who had left those footprints? The Southern Heaven Demon Empress? Or one of the Dark Heaven masters under her command?

[P108]
I thought it over, then shook my head.

[P109]
I wasn’t some old veteran of Murim. These clues could tell me only so much. Namho had encountered a wealth of information as an agent of the Hidden Shadow Pavilion, but his knowledge concerned fiends’ faces and other outward features.

[P110]
*I need someone with both the martial arts and the experience to read this scene.*

[P111]
Only two names came to mind. One belonged to a man I couldn’t bring myself to trust.

[P112]
I turned to Yayul Mok.

[P113]
“When will Great Hero Yayul arrive?”

[P114]
“I’ve already sent word. He should be on his way with the other chieftains by now.”

[P115]
That was good news. I made sure Heugung’s wrist was where I’d found it, to preserve the scene, then sniffed the pouch Yohi had left behind. The silk had split along one side, and only the faintest trace of scent remained—almost nothing.

[P116]
*I’ll find out what happened. No matter what.*

[P117]
Just then, a commotion broke out beyond the pavilion.

[P118]
“Father must have arrived at last,” Yayul Mok said. “He may be able to identify the attacker.”

[P119]
But before I even stepped outside, I knew he was wrong.

[P120]
The Beast Miao King wasn’t the first to arrive. And the person being named as the culprit was someone I hadn’t expected.

[P121]
“The guilty man is coming out on his own.”

[P122]
The moment I heard Baeksang’s flat voice, I understood.

[P123]
Baeksang and the Beast Miao King weren’t the only Supreme Peak masters in Nanman capable of doing this.
```

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

## English and Markdown

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
